sections.title: Cape plant
sections.text: Retzia capensis is a small, hairy, rosette-forming perennial endemic to South Africa's southwestern Cape. It grows to about 10 cm tall. Its crowded leaves are roughly 3–7 cm long.

sections.title: Tubular flowers
sections.text: The axillary corollas are orange-red with dark tips and measure about 45–55 mm long. The plate's narrow dark-tipped flowers, hairy leaves and capsule match the published description. No edible use or toxicity was confirmed in the sources consulted.

sections.title: Habitat
sections.text: It grows in damp, mossy rocky places in the southwestern Cape. This compact rock-dwelling species is unlike the tree-sized plants in the nearby oak entries.
